nameOrigin: a structure protruding from a fortification
common dinosaur suffix, from the Greek for 'tooth'

pokedexEntries.di: Any frontal attack is repulsed. It is a docile Pokémon that feeds on grass and berries.

pokedexEntries.prl: When attacked, they form a wall with their shieldlike faces to protect their young.

pokedexEntries.pt: When they lined up side by side, no foe could break through. They shielded their young in that way.

pokedexEntries.hgss: When attacked, they form a wall. Their rock-hard faces serve to protect them from the attacks.

pokedexEntries.as: Any frontal attack is repulsed. It is a docile Pokémon that feeds on grass and berries.

pokedexEntries.su: While it can guard against any sort of attack from the front, it is left without recourse when attacked from behind.

pokedexEntries.mo: It lived in the same environments as Rampardos. Their fossils have been found together—seemingly from after they’d fought to the finish.

pokedexEntries.us: The bones of its face are huge and hard, so they were mistaken for its spine until after this Pokémon was successfully restored.

pokedexEntries.um: This Pokémon is from roughly 100 million years ago. Its terrifyingly tough face is harder than steel.

pokedexEntries.bd: Any frontal attack is repulsed. It is a docile Pokémon that feeds on grass and berries.

pokedexEntries.shp: When attacked, they form a wall with their shield-like faces to protect their young.

pokedexEntries.la: Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.

pokedexEntries.sc: While it can guard against any sort of attack from the front, it is left without recourse when attacked from behind.

pokedexEntries.vi: Bastiodon live in herds. When assaulted by enemies, they line up side by side and use their hard faces to block attacks.
